column1: # Hand-written algorithmic code ONLY. Preflight (check 21) walks kernel/** and
# fails on any module not listed here, and on any listed module whose path does
# The kernel crate owns two things: the GENERATED port it includes at build time,
# and the hand-written modules that give that shape behaviour. Only the second is
# listed here. `lib` is the crate root that includes the generated port, which is
# why it is listed even though almost all of it is `include!`.
# The generated port is NOT here on purpose: it is a projection of the sheets and
# is regenerated on every build, so there is no checked-in file for this allowlist
# to gate (D6). What the allowlist gates is the part a human typed.

column6: the kernel crate root: includes the generated port from $OUT_DIR and declares the modules below
mirrors Terraria.Utils.ParseArguements; inline tests cover the flag, value and duplicate rules (dec020)
mirrors Terraria.Program.LaunchGame as far as a stub port allows; inline tests
the MDD 5.6 emit shim: runs the pipeline, emits the port and the per-sheet modules, hash-gated
the server's entry path, hand-written from the decompiled C#: accept, packet framing, the Hello handshake, the three state guards; inline socket tests
the hostile-input regression suite: real sockets, one bad client at a time, asserting the server is never tricked into serving and is still alive and accepting afterwards

first slice of the `player` unit (rank 1 by measured workload): the field sanitisation the C# applies to SyncPlayer(4), the first message a client sends after PlayerInfo (MessageBuffer.cs:296-305); the skin bound is derived from the id table's own highest member rather than typed

the first slice of the world work and the one with no conflicts: reads a .wld container and world header, checked against a REAL world file by asserting the container ends exactly on positions[0], which is the same check the C# makes (WorldFile.cs:1771)

the tile section decoder (WorldFile.cs:2524 LoadWorldTiles), including the run-length encoding in the header byte's high two bits; checked against real worlds by asserting the section ends exactly on positions[2]. WallID.Count and TileID.Sets.SaveSlopes are parameters because the book carries no value for either

the five message bodies that hand a client the world: WorldData(7), StatusTextSize(9), TileSection(10), TileFrameSection(11) and PlayerSpawn(12). The values are not re-typed: they are the world header and flag section reordered onto the wire, and the one place the two orders differ (the 13 background styles) is pinned by a test that would fail on a copy. Message 11 is implemented and labelled as unreachable, because nothing in the native server sends it.
